requirement: Describe a prospective, randomized, open-label, two-arm parallel hospital trial comparing SafeBreak Vascular added to electronically pumped peripheral-IV care with standard peripheral-IV care, with follow-up through IV discontinuation, discharge or seven days.

evidence.text: The synopsis states a prospective randomized trial, identifies the device and standard-care control, and follows participants to IV discontinuation, discharge or seven days.

requirement: Specify the randomization sequence, 1:1 allocation ratio, any unit or ward stratification, allocation concealment, timing relative to PIV placement and safeguards against enrolling the same patient or multiple catheters more than once.

evidence.text: The protocol says randomized and targets 73 per arm but gives no sequence, concealment or stratification details and excludes patients with two or more concurrent PIVs.

requirement: Restrict eligibility to adults in the named inpatient units who have or need one peripheral IV expected to last at least 24 hours and receive pump-based intermittent or continuous infusion; exclude gravity tubing, concurrent multiple PIVs, comfort-only care, COVID-19 and conflicting study enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol enumerates inpatient units, adult consent, PIV duration and infusion requirements plus exclusions for gravity tubing, multiple PIVs, comfort care, COVID-19 and other studies.

requirement: Operationalize the primary endpoint as participant-level therapy-delay time attributable to qualifying PIV mechanical complications during a defined 24-hour exposure period, specifying start/stop timestamps, whether zero-event patients contribute zero, aggregation across multiple events and inclusion of SafeBreak separations or failures.

evidence.text: The protocol calls the primary endpoint time to restart therapy following a catheter mechanical complication.
The plan instead describes average delay per 24 hours and includes SafeBreak separations and device failures, without a complete derivation.

requirement: State the noninferiority null and alternative on an explicit direction and estimand, provide a clinically justified noninferiority margin in time units, and define the confidence-interval decision rule; a named noninferiority rank-sum test without a margin is not executable.

evidence.text: The primary objective is noninferiority of therapy delay, followed conditionally by superiority.
The plan names a noninferiority Wilcoxon rank-sum test but gives no margin, hypotheses or interval rule.

requirement: Gate superiority testing on successful noninferiority using the same prespecified primary endpoint and population hierarchy, and define whether superiority is tested only after both primary intention-to-treat and per-protocol noninferiority conclusions agree.

evidence.text: The protocol asks first whether delay is noninferior and, if so, whether SafeBreak is superior.

requirement: Define a randomized intention-to-treat or full-analysis population as a required primary or co-primary noninferiority analysis, preserving assigned group despite nonplacement, separation, replacement, cross-over or early discontinuation.

evidence.text: The study is randomized but supplies no analysis-population definition.
The plan names only a per-protocol population, which is insufficient by itself for a noninferiority claim.

requirement: Define the per-protocol population prospectively, including minimum device exposure, qualifying PIV, major deviations, prohibited concurrent lines, allocation errors, device nonplacement and early exit, and require concordance with the randomized-population analysis for noninferiority.

evidence.text: The plan says the analysis population will be per protocol but gives no eligibility or deviation rules.

requirement: Replace or fully specify the proposed rank-sum approach with an estimator and confidence interval aligned to the primary delay estimand and noninferiority margin, addressing zero inflation, unequal observation time, repeated complications and skewness rather than reporting only a Wilcoxon p-value.

evidence.text: The plan proposes noninferiority and standard Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for average 24-hour delay but supplies no effect estimator, interval, margin or event-aggregation treatment.

requirement: State the primary estimand with eligible inpatient population, assigned device strategy, therapy-delay variable and 24-hour or seven-day horizon, between-group summary measure and strategies for discharge, IV discontinuation, device replacement, death, transfer and competing clinical interruption.

evidence.text: The protocol defines groups and variable follow-up to discharge, IV discontinuation or seven days but gives no estimand.

requirement: Define each secondary mechanical-complication endpoint separately, including dislodgement, infiltration, phlebitis, occlusion, infection, blood or fluid spillage and PIV restart, with adjudication rules, patient-versus-event denominator, recurrent-event handling and exposure time.

evidence.text: The protocol lists mechanical complications, blood loss, fluid spillage and PIV restarts without operational definitions.

requirement: Match the analysis to the secondary endpoint: use cumulative incidence or survival methods only for time to first complication with a stated time origin and competing events, participant-level risk methods for any-event incidence, and an exposure-adjusted recurrent-event model for counts; do not call a Kaplan-Meier estimate a proportion without defining time.

evidence.text: The plan interchangeably proposes Kaplan-Meier proportions, chi-square/Fisher tests and Poisson regression without tying them to time-to-first, participant incidence or event counts.

requirement: Do not ignore nonendpoint missing data wholesale; define missing primary timestamps, incomplete IV checks, unknown complication type, missing covariates and loss of observation, report reasons by arm and distinguish administrative censoring from informative early exit.

evidence.text: The plan states that missing data that is not endpoint data will be ignored and permits censoring at early exit without further assumptions.

requirement: Add noninferiority sensitivity analyses for missing delay times and informative discharge or IV discontinuation, including conservative arm-specific imputations or tipping points, plus concordant randomized and per-protocol results.

evidence.text: Follow-up ends variably at discharge, IV discontinuation or seven days, creating potentially informative missing exposure.
No noninferiority missing-data sensitivity is specified.

requirement: Control type-I error for the noninferiority-then-superiority sequence and define the status of multiple secondary complication outcomes, analysis populations and alternative tests; label all ungated secondary comparisons exploratory with confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol states a conditional noninferiority then superiority objective and multiple secondary complications but no multiplicity strategy.

requirement: Reproduce the 66-per-arm noninferiority calculation by supplying the missing margin, delay distribution or variance, event prevalence, sided alpha, test or interval method and expected analyzable rate; verify that adding 10% yields the stated 73 per arm and 146 total without substituting actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol targets 146 total, 73 per arm, with 10% allowance.
The plan states 66 per arm for 80% power at alpha 0.05 but omits the margin and other calculation inputs.

requirement: Define the safety population as all participants exposed to assigned PIV care and summarize adverse events and device deficiencies by arm, including separation, device failure, blood loss, fluid spillage, infection, severity, relatedness, serious events and twice-daily surveillance duration.

evidence.text: The research team evaluates all participants at least twice daily for adverse events and safety concerns.

requirement: Specify one- versus two-sided alpha for noninferiority and superiority, confidence levels, effect measures and software, and report estimates and intervals rather than relying on p-values alone.

evidence.text: The plan gives alpha 0.05 but no sidedness, confidence level, effect estimand or software.

requirement: Prespecify handling of hospital unit and baseline infusion characteristics, retaining randomization strata if any and using adjustment or stratified summaries for unit, infusion type, expected catheter duration and baseline risk without outcome-driven covariate selection.

evidence.text: Participants arise from several inpatient units with intermittent or continuous infusions and varying anticipated duration.

requirement: Keep the three-page statistical-plan synopsis annotation-only and expose only the four-page protocol synopsis in protocol-only generation; preserve the shared HHC-2020-0086 identity and 2020-10-13 during-recruitment approval evidence.

evidence.text: The protocol synopsis prints HHC-2020-0086 and IRB approval date 2020-10-13.
The separate statistical-plan synopsis prints the same IRB identity and approval date.
